I spoke to you previously about a number of things.
# ASSISTANT
Update your test fixture to include 'headers={'Origin': 'http://www.example.com'}' in the connect method. That should simulate the browser environment correctly.

I previously resolved CORS configuration issues in my FastAPI application by reordering middleware in main.py to place CORSMiddleware before my custom BaseHTTPMiddleware, updating settings.py to include 'PUT' and 'DELETE' methods, and removing manual CORS headers from nginx.conf. I also resolved CI regressions in tests/test_middleware.py by updating the TestClient base_url and consolidating the app instance into a single pytest fixture in conftest.py. Additionally, I implemented DebugMiddleware for logging and configured ProxyHeadersMiddleware for production, verifying these changes in tests/test_middleware_cors.py using httpx.

Following the closure of issue #1663, I investigated intermittent 500 errors under high load, specifically an AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'headers' in starlette.middleware.cors.CORSMiddleware.dispatch. I addressed this concurrency bug by implementing a manual middleware fix in middleware_utils.py, which I validated using a pytest-asyncio test case with asyncio.gather to simulate concurrent requests. This fix passed 100 consecutive iterations, eliminated the 500 errors, and increased throughput by 15 percent. I have since finalized a regression test in tests/test_cors.py and documented the risks of shared state in middleware within CONTRIBUTING.md.

I am now moving the manual middleware implementation into a helper function in app/utils.py to improve maintainability. Finally, I am investigating why WebSocket endpoints in app/api/ws.py are still throwing origin errors, as I suspect CORSMiddleware may not be intended for WebSocket connections.

# USER
Refactoring now. I'll call it 'verify_origin'. It will accept the 'scope' and the allowed list, raising a 'WebSocketDisconnect' if validation fails.
